status_summary: The recommended statute has been introduced but not enacted: S. 1496, the New Markets for State-Inspected Meat and Poultry Act of 2025, was introduced on 2025-04-10 and referred to the Agriculture Committee, and no committee action, House companion or Administration statement on the bill was found. In parallel, USDA added Georgia to the existing Cooperative Interstate Shipment program on 2026-07-27, bringing it to 11 states, and Executive Order 14424 (signed 2026-09-04, published 2026-09-10) directs USDA to expand state participation in cooperative inspection programs and to report within 60 days on statutory and regulatory barriers to interstate sale of state-inspected meat. The order does not name or propose the bill. Because the recommendation is to promote legislation and the only legislative step is an introduction, the record is scored as proposed; the executive steps widen interstate access within current law for participating states.

timeline.event: S. 1496, the New Markets for State-Inspected Meat and Poultry Act of 2025, was introduced by Sen. Rounds with nine original cosponsors and referred to the Senate Agriculture Committee; it would strike the intrastate-only limit in the federal meat and poultry inspection acts.
USDA and Georgia finalized a Cooperative Interstate Shipment agreement, bringing the program to 11 states.

Executive Order 14424 was signed, directing USDA to increase state participation in state and cooperative inspection programs and to report within 60 days on remaining statutory and regulatory barriers to interstate sale of state-inspected meat; it was published on 2026-09-10.

title: Promote legislation to allow state-inspected meat and poultry to cross state lines
uncertainties: No House companion to S. 1496 and no committee action were found in a search of 2026 coverage. The executive order text was read and does not name the bill or propose legislation; whether its 60-day reports (due about 2026-11-03) were delivered or published was not found. No provision on state-inspected interstate sale was seen in the visible part of the CRS 2026 farm bill comparison, which was only partly read. The Cooperative Interstate Shipment program has existed since 2012, so the 2026 addition is an expansion of an existing route. The PRIME Act (H.R. 4700, introduced 2025-07-23) concerns custom-exempt slaughter sold within a state and is related background, not the interstate recommendation; its text was not reopened in review. GovInfo BILLSTATUS (checked 2026-10-24) lists 2025-04-10 as the latest action on S. 1496, with no companion bill, so the absence of committee action is now confirmed from a primary source. Whether the House-passed H.R. 7567 (2026-04-30) or the Senate Agriculture Committee's farm bill (reported by trade press as advancing 12 to 11 on 2026-09-16) contains a state-inspected interstate provision was not established; a press comparison of the two bills showed no readable detail on meat inspection. The EO 14424 reports due about 2026-11-03 had not appeared in searches as of 2026-10-24.
